lines.speaker: momo
lines.text: Can I ask you something about telescopes?

lines.speaker: momo
lines.text: Why does a telescope show things we cannot see?

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: Its big lens or mirror gathers far more light than your eye can.

lines.speaker: momo
lines.text: So it is more about light than zoom?

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: Mostly, yes. More light means fainter things become visible.

lines.speaker: momo
lines.text: Then why do big telescopes look so huge?

lines.speaker: ravi
lines.text: A wider mirror catches more light, so astronomers build them wide.
